Analysis.description: An analysis: the files it reads, the artefacts it makes and the decisions it makes along the way. It is the content of an `astra.yaml` file.

analyses.description: The analyses this analysis uses, keyed by the id it addresses them by.

container.description: The default container of the analysis's recipes: an image, or a Containerfile it is built from.

decisions.description: The choices the analysis makes, keyed by id.

description.description: What the analysis does, in free prose.

findings.description: What the analysis concludes, as insights keyed by id.

inputs.description: The files the analysis reads, keyed by id.

label.description: A short display name for the analysis.

outputs.description: The artefacts the analysis makes, keyed by id. There is at least one.

prior_insights.description: What earlier work establishes and the analysis builds on, as insights keyed by id. Options cite them in their `insights`.

spec_version.description: The version of the ASTRA specification the document is written against, such as `0.1.0`.

tags.description: Keywords for grouping and finding the analysis.

universes.description: The universes of the analysis, and the universes of other analyses it imports, keyed by id. An import has an `analysis` and a `universe`.

Analysis.title: Analysis

AnalysisDeclaration__identifier_optional.description: An analysis that this analysis uses, found by exactly one of `path` and `url`. Its elements are addressed through the declaration's id, as `<declaration>.<element>`.

commit.description: The full id of the commit the declared analysis is read at. A declaration with a `url` has one; with a `path`, it declares the analysis at that path as it was at that commit.

path.description: The directory of the declared analysis's `astra.yaml`, relative to the folder of this `astra.yaml`, with `/` between folders. It is non-empty and doesn't start with `/`.

url.description: Where git fetches another repository from, as a remote with no ASCII space or control character, in one of two forms: `scheme://` and at least one character, where the scheme is an ASCII letter followed by any ASCII letters, digits, `+`, `.` and `-`, such as `https://example.org/remote.git` or `file:///srv/remote.git`; or scp-like, `[user@]host:path`, where `host`, `path` and any `user` are non-empty, `user` and `host` hold no `/`, `@` or `:`, and the value doesn't start with a scheme and `://`, such as `git@example.org:remote.git`. The declared analysis is the one at the top level of that repository, at `commit`.

AnalysisDeclaration__identifier_optional.title: AnalysisDeclaration

AnalysisView.description: One analysis of the stack: its file as written, and its addresses resolved.

address.description: The ids of the declarations by which the driving analysis first reaches the analysis, joined by `.`, such as `stage.inner`. The driving analysis's is the empty string.

commit.description: The full id of the commit the analysis is read at. Left out for an analysis read in the working tree.

fields.description: The content of the analysis's `astra.yaml`, as written.

file.description: The analysis's `astra.yaml`, as a path from the top of the tree it is read in.

folder.description: The analysis's folder, as a path from the top of the repository it is read in or, read in the working tree, from the top of the driving analysis's working tree. The top itself is the empty string.

refs.description: Every address the file writes, in the order of their places.

url.description: The URL of the remote the analysis is read from, if any.

AnalysisView.title: AnalysisView

active.description: Whether the decision is active in the universe. Left out where its `when` tests a decision the universe doesn't set.

analysis.description: The analysis the decision is in.

selected.description: The id of the option the universe selects. Left out where it selects none.

Decision__identifier_optional.description: A choice the analysis makes between options, such as which method to use.

label.description: A short display name for the decision.

options.description: The options the decision chooses between, keyed by id. There is at least one.

rationale.description: Why the analysis makes this decision, in free prose.

tags.description: Keywords for grouping and finding the decision.

when.description: The conditions under which the decision is active. It is active only when every condition holds.

Decision__identifier_optional.title: Decision

Element.description: An element of an analysis: what an address resolves to. Two addresses that resolve to one element are two spellings of it.

analysis.description: The analysis the element is in.

id.description: The element's id in its analysis.

Element.title: Element

ElementKind.description: The kind of element an address resolves to.
ElementKind.title: ElementKind

Evidence.description: What a claim rests on: a published work, cited by its `doi`, or an output, cited as an `artifact`. It has exactly one of the two, and a `version` only with a `doi`.

artifact.description: A reference to the cited output, written as in an output's `inputs`. It may pin the output to a universe, the one the claim is about, such as `output1#u1`.

doi.description: The DOI name of the cited work, under the `10` directory: `10.`, the registrant code, `/` and a non-empty suffix, such as `10.5555/12345678`.

location.description: The place in the cited work or output the claim rests on, such as `page=6`.

quote.description: The passage of the cited work or output the claim rests on. With a `location`, the passage is sought within that place.

version.description: The version of the cited work, counted from 1, such as `2` for the second version of an arXiv paper.

Evidence.title: Evidence

FragmentSelector.description: A place in the cited work or output, given as a fragment identifier in the syntax `conforms_to` names, such as `row=5-7` in a CSV (RFC 7111). Without `conforms_to`, it is a PDF fragment identifier (RFC 8118 §3), such as `page=6`, with pages counted from 1.

conforms_to.description: The IRI of the specification of the fragment syntax `value` follows, as W3C Web Annotation gives it, such as `http://tools.ietf.org/rfc/rfc7111` for a CSV. Without it, `value` is a PDF fragment identifier (RFC 8118).

value.description: The fragment identifier, without the leading `#`, such as `page=6`. It is non-empty, holds no ASCII space or control character and none of `"`, `#`, `<`, `>`, `[`, `\`, `]`, `^`, the backtick, `{`, `|` and `}`, and has `%` only before two hex digits.

FragmentSelector.title: FragmentSelector

Identity.description: What an analysis is known by: its folder and the commit it is read at. One folder at one commit is one analysis however it is declared.

commit.description: The full id of the commit the analysis is read at. Left out for an analysis read in the working tree.

folder.description: The analysis's folder, as a path from the top of the repository it is read in or, read in the working tree, from the top of the driving analysis's working tree. The top itself is the empty string.

Identity.title: Identity

Input__identifier_optional.description: A file the analysis reads, tracked in git with it and named by its path.

description.description: What the input's data is, in free prose.

label.description: A short display name for the input.

path.description: The path of the input's file, relative to the folder of the `astra.yaml`, with `/` between folders. It is non-empty and doesn't start with `/`.

tags.description: Keywords for grouping and finding the input.

Input__identifier_optional.title: Input

Insight__identifier_optional.description: A claim backed by evidence: as a prior insight, what earlier work establishes and the analysis builds on; as a finding, what the analysis concludes.

description.description: The reasoning behind the claim, in free prose.

evidence.description: What the claim rests on, as a list. There is at least one.

label.description: A short display name for the insight.

scope.description: The conditions under which the claim holds, in free prose.

tags.description: Keywords for grouping and finding the insight.

Insight__identifier_optional.title: Insight

Option__identifier_optional.description: One of the options a decision chooses between.

description.description: What the option is, in free prose.

excluded.description: Why the option is ruled out. An option with a reason is excluded: no effective selection selects it.

incompatible_with.description: The options that are never selected together with this option.

insights.description: The ids of the prior insights that support the option.

label.description: A short display name for the option.

requires.description: The options that are also selected whenever this option is.

tags.description: Keywords for grouping and finding the option.

Option__identifier_optional.title: Option

active.description: Whether the output is active in the universe. Left out where its `when` tests a decision the universe doesn't set.

analysis.description: The analysis the output is in.

OutputType.description: The kind of artefact an output is.
OutputType.title: OutputType

Output__identifier_optional.description: An artefact the analysis makes, such as a metric, a figure or a table: what it is, what it is made from, and how.

decisions.description: The addresses of the decisions whose option the output is made with directly, not through what it reads: a different option for any of them, in the universe being built, can give a different result.

description.description: What the output is, in free prose.

format.description: How the output's artefact is encoded, as a lowercase token: the extension of its results' files, without the leading dot, such as `png`, `csv` or `parquet`.

inputs.description: What the output is made from, in order: references to inputs and outputs of the analysis or of analyses it declares. A reference can be pinned to a universe with `#`.

label.description: A short display name for the output.

tags.description: Keywords for grouping and finding the output.

type.description: The kind of artefact the output is.

when.description: The conditions under which the output is active. It is active only when every condition holds.

Output__identifier_optional.title: Output

Place.description: Where one name of a planned result puts it, in the folder of the analysis the result belongs to.

address.description: The name, then, for a result built in a universe, `#` and that universe's own id, such as `subanalysis.output1#u1`.

bytes.description: The default place of the result's bytes, as a path from the top of the tree its analysis is read in.

name.description: The result's name: its output's id after the ids of the driven declarations that lead to it from the analysis it belongs to, such as `subanalysis.output1`.

record.description: The place of the result's record, as a path from the top of the tree its analysis is read in.

Place.title: Place

Read.description: One entry of an output's `inputs`, and what a planned result reads through it: an input's file, or another planned result's bytes.

commit.description: The full id of the commit `path` is read at. Left out for the working tree.

entry.description: The entry exactly as the output's `inputs` lists it.

path.description: The input's file, or the default place of the bytes of the result read, as a path from the top of the tree it is read in.

result.description: The planned result read, as its index in the `results` that hold this one. Left out for an input.

Read.title: Read

Recipe.description: How an output is made: a `command` and the context it runs in (`resources`, `container`). What the output is made from, the decisions it is made with and when it is active are the output's `inputs`, `decisions` and `when`; the command reaches the inputs and decisions through its placeholders.

command.description:
The POSIX shell command that makes the output, such as `python src/output1.py`. It is a template. Read from the left, `{{` stands for a literal `{` and `}}` for a literal `}`, and any other `{` opens a placeholder, which ends at the next `}`. A runner substitutes each placeholder, and each `{{` and `}}`, before running the command:

  {inputs.<entry>}     the path of what an entry of the output's
                       `inputs` names, with <entry> written
                       exactly as the entry is, dots and `#`
                       included, as in
                       {inputs.subanalysis.output1#u1}
  {decisions.<entry>}  the id of the option selected for the
                       decision an entry of the output's
                       `decisions` names, with <entry> written
                       exactly as the entry is, as in
                       {decisions.subanalysis.decision1}
  {inputs}             the paths of all the output's inputs, in
                       the order of `inputs`, separated by spaces
  {output}             the path the result is written to

Every brace belongs to a `{{`, a `}}` or a placeholder, every placeholder takes one of these forms, and the <entry> of an {inputs.<entry>} or {decisions.<entry>} is an entry of the output's `inputs` or `decisions`, exactly as written.

container.description: The container the recipe runs in: an image, or a Containerfile it is built from.

resources.description: The compute resources the recipe asks for.

Recipe.title: Recipe

Reference.description: One address written in an `astra.yaml`, and what it resolves to.

negated.description: Whether a condition starts with `~`. Left out where it doesn't.

option.description: The id of the option a condition, an option reference or a selection names.

pin.description: The universe a reference's pin names.

pointer.description: A JSON Pointer to where the address is written in the file: the value or, for a key of a universe's `decisions`, the entry.

Reference.title: Reference

Resources.description: The compute resources a recipe asks for.

cpus.description: The number of CPU cores the recipe asks for, which may be fractional, such as 0.5.

disk.description: The disk space the recipe asks for, as free text, such as `10GB`.

gpus.description: The number of GPUs the recipe asks for.

memory.description: The memory the recipe asks for, as free text, such as `4GB`.

time_limit.description: The longest the recipe may run, as free text, such as `2h`.

Resources.title: Resources

Result.description: A planned result: one output's, in the universe it is built in or, for an output built once, once.

decisions.description: What the result is made with: one item for each entry of its output's `decisions`, in their order.

inputs.description: What the result reads: one item for each entry of its output's `inputs`, in their order.

names.description: The result's names, one for each driven chain that reaches it.

output.description: The output the result is of.

owner.description: The analysis the result belongs to: the one whose universe builds it or, for an output built once, the one whose output it is.

places.description: The result's places, one for each of its names, in their order.

universe.description: The id of the universe the result is built in, one of its owner's. Left out for an output built once.

Result.title: Result

Selected.description: One entry of an output's `decisions`, and the option a planned result is made with for it.

entry.description: The entry exactly as the output's `decisions` lists it.

option.description: The id of the option selected where the result is built. Left out where none is.

Selected.title: Selected

TextQuoteSelector.description: A passage of the cited work or output, quoted exactly, with the text just before and after it to tell it apart where the same words occur more than once.

exact.description: The passage, exactly as the cited work or output writes it.

prefix.description: The text that comes just before the passage.

suffix.description: The text that comes just after the passage.

TextQuoteSelector.title: TextQuoteSelector

UniverseView.description: A universe in which results are built, and the stack as it is there.

analysis.description: The analysis whose universe it is.

built.description: The analyses built in the universe: its own, then each that its analysis's universes drive.

decisions.description: Each decision of the analyses built in the universe.

id.description: The universe's id in its analysis.

outputs.description: Each output of the analyses built in the universe.

UniverseView.title: UniverseView

Universe__identifier_optional.description: An entry of `universes`: a universe of the analysis, a selection of one option for every active decision of the analysis and of every analysis reached through a declaration that the analysis's universes drive, or an import, which has an `analysis` and a `universe`, names one of another analysis's universes and selects nothing. A universe's effective selection is the effective selection of the universe it is derived from, if any, with its own `decisions` written over it decision by decision and every inherited selection of a decision that isn't active in the result dropped, so a universe that switches a decision on must set it.

analysis.description: For an import, the address of the declaration that leads to the analysis whose universe it imports, through as many declarations as lead to it, such as `subanalysis` or `stage.inner`.

additionalProperties.description: The id of the option selected for the decision.

decisions.description: The options the universe selects, as `<decision>: <option>`, one key per decision. Each key is the id of a decision of the analysis or, for a decision of another analysis, a flat key: the decision's address through the declarations, `<declaration>.<decision>`, such as `subanalysis.decision1`, or another spelling of that address, through no declaration back to an analysis already on its chain.

derived_from.description: The id of another universe of the analysis, never an import, whose effective selection this universe's effective selection is built on, so that this universe gives only the decisions it changes. The universe inherits only that selection.

description.description: What the universe is, in free prose.

label.description: A short display name for the universe.

tags.description: Keywords for grouping and finding the universe.

universe.description: For an import, the id of the universe it imports: a universe of the analysis that `analysis` leads to, never an import of that analysis.

Universe__identifier_optional.title: Universe

description: An analysis and its stack, as tools read them.

analyses.description: The analyses of the stack, the driving analysis first.

results.description: The planned results, each after every result it reads.

root.description: The driving analysis's `astra.yaml`, as a path from the top of the repository that holds it.

shape.description: The name and version of this shape.

universes.description: The universes in which results are built, the driving analysis's first.
